metadata.research_goal: Synthesize credible cycling handling and safety guidance into backend-ready records for braking, cornering, descending, climbing, shifting, cadence, road awareness, group riding, bike checks, wet and loose-surface skills, beginner progression, traffic-safe advancement, and assessment signals.

source_refs.title: Learning the Cycling Skills for Your First Criterium
Learning Essential Skills for Your First Mountain Bike Race
Riding in a group - Top 10 tips
How to climb - 10 top tips for beginners
Bicycle Safety: Bike Safety Tips for Kids and Adults
Seven Smart Routes to Bicycle Safety for Adults

key_concepts.name: Handling skill gates speed and intensity
key_concepts.summary: Fast descents, race-like cornering, and pack riding should be introduced only after the rider shows predictable bike control in lower-risk environments.
key_concepts.backend_use: Gate high-speed, group, criterium, and descent workouts behind observable handling readiness.

key_concepts.name: Traffic exposure progresses by road complexity
key_concepts.summary: Safe cycling progression moves from traffic-free control skills to simple roads and junctions, then to busier, faster, or multi-lane environments.
key_concepts.backend_use: Assign route and traffic complexity by level rather than by fitness alone.

key_concepts.name: Braking is a traction and body-position skill
key_concepts.summary: Braking effectiveness depends on using both brakes appropriately, moving body weight to preserve tire grip, and avoiding panic inputs.
key_concepts.backend_use: Teach braking as a drillable skill before descents, traffic rides, group rides, and wet-condition riding.

key_concepts.name: Cornering uses a limited traction budget
key_concepts.summary: Braking, steering, leaning, pedaling, and surface friction compete for grip; beginners should slow before the turn and keep mid-corner inputs smooth.
key_concepts.backend_use: Flag mid-corner braking, pedal strike risk, and wet or loose surfaces as regression triggers.

key_concepts.name: Vision drives balance and line choice
key_concepts.summary: Looking through the turn, through the group, and ahead for hazards gives the rider time to steer, brake, signal, and choose a safer line.
key_concepts.backend_use: Use gaze and scan behavior as assessment signals for cornering, group riding, traffic, and MTB skills.

key_concepts.name: Predictability is a safety behavior
key_concepts.summary: Riders reduce risk by holding a straight line, signaling intentions, obeying traffic controls, communicating hazards, and avoiding sudden speed changes.
key_concepts.backend_use: Promote riders only when control is predictable to other road users and riders.

key_concepts.name: Cadence and gearing are control tools
key_concepts.summary: Gears should help maintain a sustainable cadence across terrain; late shifts under heavy load increase loss-of-control, dropped-chain, and fatigue risks.
key_concepts.backend_use: Connect shifting skill to climbing, group smoothness, knee-load risk, and beginner comfort.

key_concepts.name: Climbing technique balances pacing, cadence, and traction
key_concepts.summary: Efficient climbing is usually seated and relaxed, with early gear choice, smooth pedaling, and traction-aware position changes on wet or loose climbs.
key_concepts.backend_use: Separate climbing skill sessions from pure power sessions and regress standing efforts when traction or control is poor.

key_concepts.name: Group riding is collective risk management
key_concepts.summary: A group rider's actions affect others; communication, steady pacing, no wheel overlap, light braking, and shared hazard calls are core safety behaviors.
key_concepts.backend_use: Require group-readiness skills before fast club rides, pacelines, criteriums, or bunch tactics.

key_concepts.name: Pre-ride checks are part of riding competence
key_concepts.summary: Tires, brakes, chain, cranks, quick releases, wheels, and a short test ride should be checked before training or travel rides.
key_concepts.backend_use: Include bike-check habit as a beginner assessment and a risk modifier after maintenance, travel, crashes, or equipment changes.

key_concepts.name: Wet and loose surfaces demand regression
key_concepts.summary: Rain, wet leaves, paint, metal, bridges, gravel, mud, and loose dirt reduce grip and require lower speed, extra stopping distance, and gentler inputs.
key_concepts.backend_use: Auto-regress skill and route prescriptions when surface or weather reduces traction.

key_concepts.name: Crash protection and visibility are baseline safety layers
key_concepts.summary: A properly fitted helmet, visible clothing or lights in low visibility, and attention to local light laws reduce severe consequences and improve detectability.
key_concepts.backend_use: Treat missing helmet or visibility equipment as a safety-blocking risk for outdoor road plans.

progression: identify front and rear brake setup before riding
practice controlled rear-only, front-only, and both-brake stops in an empty area
add emergency stops with hips back, arms braced, heels down, and eyes forward
add braking before turns and descents
add wet or loose-surface braking only at reduced speed
assessment_signals: stops inside a marked zone without skidding
keeps head up and bike straight
releases rear pressure when skid begins
regress_if: cannot stop predictably from moderate speed

progression: wide slow turns on flat traffic-free ground
cone slalom with eyes to next cone
brake before the turn and release pressure through the apex
inside pedal up on tighter road turns
outside-pedal pressure and relaxed upper body
road-speed corners only after line holding is consistent
assessment_signals: holds a smooth line without abrupt steering
sets up wide enough before entry
does not pedal-strike or brake sharply mid-corner

progression: confirm brakes, tires, and wheels before descending practice
start on short low-grade descents with clear sight lines
practice hands in stable braking position and relaxed elbows
control speed before bends
add linked corners only when braking and line choice remain calm
add longer or steeper descents after rider stays relaxed and recovers well
assessment_signals: keeps body low, stable, and relaxed
regress_if: entering corners faster than visible stopping distance allows

progression: select easy gears before gradient increases
maintain sustainable cadence and talking-level effort on beginner climbs
stay seated with quiet upper body on longer climbs
add brief standing efforts after rider can shift up and avoid rear-wheel kickback
practice traction climbs seated and forward on slippery surfaces
add steep or repeated climbs after pacing and gear selection are reliable
assessment_signals: keeps relaxed grip and stable torso
can crest without abrupt stop or chain drop
regress_if: standing causes rear-wheel kickback near others

progression: learn easier versus harder gear effect on flat terrain
use cadence awareness by sensor or timed pedal counts
hold a comfortable steady cadence on flat roads
shift early before hills, stops, and accelerations
practice increasing cadence before shifting harder during accelerations
use easier gearing to avoid excessive low-cadence load
regress_if: looks down at drivetrain in traffic
cannot restart because gear is too hard

progression: practice straight-line riding in a narrow lane
practice shoulder scans while maintaining line
add one-hand riding and hand signals in a parking lot
add left-right-left checks before entering roads
add simple lane-position changes on quiet roads
add busier roads only when scans and signals do not disrupt line
assessment_signals: signals before turns or lane changes
keeps both attention and bike control
checks ahead and behind before avoiding hazards
regress_if: uses headphones or phone while riding in traffic

progression: solo straight-line, braking, scanning, and signaling competence
side-by-side riding in controlled setting
low-speed proximity drills on grass or empty roads
steady small-group ride with generous spacing
single paceline with light speed changes
faster group or criterium only after rider holds line under fatigue
assessment_signals: looks through group rather than only at nearest wheel
uses light braking or wind resistance to adjust spacing

progression: identify reduced-grip hazards before ride
lower speed and increase following distance
brake earlier and more gently while upright
avoid abrupt steering or pedaling over slippery paint, metal, leaves, mud, or gravel
choose better-traction lines
add technical wet or loose practice only with skill supervision and conservative speed
assessment_signals: keeps bike upright over slick hazards where possible
regress_if: corners aggressively on paint or metal
rides soft trails that should be avoided

progression: check tire inflation and visible tire condition
check brake function and lever travel
check chain and crank security
check quick releases or thru-axles
check helmet fit, lights, reflectors, supplies, and phone for route context
perform a short slow test ride before leaving
assessment_signals: detects obvious brake, tire, chain, or wheel problems
does not start group or traffic ride with unsafe equipment

progression: traffic-free start, stop, turn, scan, signal, and obstacle drills
quiet road with simple starts, stops, parked-car clearance, and side-road awareness
simple junctions with moderate traffic
planned short journeys with visible gear and predictable lane position
busier or faster roads only after Level 2-style competence is demonstrated
assessment_signals: checks behind and signals before moving

tactical_rules.rule: Reduce speed before initiating a turn; avoid hard braking once leaned over unless needed for safety.
tactical_rules.why: Separating braking from cornering preserves traction and makes the line more predictable.
tactical_rules.progression_gate: Rider can complete flat cone turns with no mid-turn panic braking.

tactical_rules.rule: Descend no faster than the rider can stop within the visible, usable road or trail ahead.
tactical_rules.why: Blind bends, debris, traffic, animals, or trail users can appear before the rider has room to react.
tactical_rules.progression_gate: Rider consistently brakes early, looks ahead, and stays relaxed on short descents.

tactical_rules.rule: When stronger or weaker than the group, adjust time at the front rather than changing the group pace.
tactical_rules.why: Pace surges and sudden slowdowns ripple through the group and increase contact risk.
tactical_rules.progression_gate: Rider can hold steady effort and rotate predictably.

tactical_rules.rule: Do not overlap the front wheel with the rear wheel ahead in normal group riding.
tactical_rules.why: A small lateral move by the rider ahead can remove the following rider's front wheel and cause a crash.
tactical_rules.progression_gate: Rider can maintain spacing without staring at the wheel ahead.

tactical_rules.rule: Communicate turns, stops, slowing, potholes, debris, and road hazards early enough for riders behind to respond.
tactical_rules.why: The front rider sees hazards first; safe groups move information backward through the line.
tactical_rules.progression_gate: Rider can signal or call hazards without swerving.

tactical_rules.rule: Do not use clip-on aerobars in group rides unless the session is specifically structured and supervised for that equipment.
tactical_rules.why: Aero positions reduce immediate brake access and fine steering control in close proximity.
tactical_rules.progression_gate: Triathlon or TT riders use normal hand positions when riding near others.

tactical_rules.rule: Use a visible, predictable lane position; when a lane is too narrow to share safely, occupying the lane may be safer than inviting a squeeze pass, subject to local law.
tactical_rules.why: Lane position should manage blind spots, hazards, parked-car doors, and overtaking risk.
tactical_rules.progression_gate: Rider can scan, signal, and hold line before changing position.

tactical_rules.rule: Obey signs, signals, road markings, and stop controls during solo and group rides.
tactical_rules.why: Predictable vehicle-like behavior reduces conflicts and prevents unsafe group-splitting decisions at intersections.
tactical_rules.progression_gate: Rider understands local traffic rules before unsupervised road routes.

tactical_rules.rule: When standing out of the saddle near others, shift slightly harder and rise smoothly to avoid rear-wheel kickback.
tactical_rules.why: Sudden speed loss or rear-wheel movement can threaten the following rider's front wheel.
tactical_rules.progression_gate: Rider practices seated-to-standing transitions alone before doing them in a group.

tactical_rules.rule: Ride open trails only, stay within limits, yield appropriately, announce passes, and expect other users around blind corners.
tactical_rules.why: Shared trail safety depends on speed control, communication, and respecting closures and surface conditions.
tactical_rules.progression_gate: Rider can stop or slow before blind trail features and pass only with communication.

tactical_rules.rule: Reduce speed and increase stopping and following distance in rain, frost, wet leaves, metal, paint, bridges, and loose gravel.
tactical_rules.why: Low-friction surfaces reduce braking and cornering margins for both the rider and nearby traffic.
tactical_rules.progression_gate: Rider demonstrates dry-condition braking and cornering competence first.

tactical_rules.rule: New group riders should start with the slowest suitable group and move up only after the pace and handling demands feel controlled.
tactical_rules.why: Underestimating the group prevents fatigue-driven mistakes and preserves learning quality.
tactical_rules.progression_gate: Rider completes multiple rides without unsafe spacing, braking, or fatigue-related errors.

physical_demands.name: Relaxed postural control
physical_demands.description: Handling requires trunk support with relaxed shoulders, elbows, hands, and jaw so the bike can move beneath the rider without overcorrection.
physical_demands.backend_implication: Add low-risk handling drills and trunk endurance before prescribing technical descents or close pack work.

physical_demands.name: Braking strength and coordination
physical_demands.description: Emergency stops require grip force, arm bracing, hip shift, heel drop, and brake modulation under time pressure.
physical_demands.backend_implication: Do not assume aerobic fitness equals stopping competence; assess braking separately.

physical_demands.name: Cadence neuromotor range
physical_demands.description: A rider needs enough coordination to pedal smoothly across comfortable, climbing, accelerating, and high-cadence contexts.
physical_demands.backend_implication: Use cadence drills as skill work, not only conditioning.

physical_demands.name: Climbing torque tolerance
physical_demands.description: Steep climbs may force lower cadence and higher pedal force, increasing knee and fatigue load if gearing and pacing are poor.
physical_demands.backend_implication: Progress climbing volume and low-cadence work conservatively, especially with knee symptoms.

physical_demands.name: Visual attention and hazard processing
physical_demands.description: Safe riders scan ahead, through groups, behind before moving, and across intersections while maintaining a stable line.
physical_demands.backend_implication: Treat attention failures and distraction as safety blockers, not minor errors.

physical_demands.name: Upper-body contact tolerance
physical_demands.description: Pack racing and tight group environments may involve incidental shoulder or elbow contact that should be absorbed without panic steering.
physical_demands.backend_implication: Introduce contact drills only after solo control is stable and only in grass or controlled low-speed settings.

physical_demands.name: Descending grip and neck load
physical_demands.description: Long descents demand sustained braking access, visual scanning, neck extension, hand comfort, and calm grip pressure.
physical_demands.backend_implication: Use shorter descents and bike-fit review when hand, neck, or shoulder symptoms appear.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Abrupt braking in a group creates a speed ripple and rear-end crash risk.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Teach anticipation, light brake modulation, wind-resistance spacing adjustments, and hazard calls.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Front-wheel overlap with the rider ahead can cause immediate loss of control if the lead rider moves laterally.
risk_flags: riding half a wheel beside the rider ahead
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Increase gap, offset safely without overlap, and practice close riding only after controlled drills.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Wet leaves, paint, metal grates, bridges, railroad tracks, gravel, mud, and potholes increase fall risk.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Slow down, keep inputs smooth, cross tracks close to 90 degrees, and increase stopping distance.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Riding without a properly fitted helmet increases consequences of a crash, especially for beginners and traffic rides.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Require properly fitted, undamaged helmet for outdoor sessions and replace after impact.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Unsafe brakes, loose wheels, poor tires, or drivetrain problems can convert normal handling demands into crashes.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Use ABC Quick Check and repair issues before riding in traffic, groups, descents, or remote areas.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Low-cadence big-gear climbing and late shifts can increase knee load and fatigue, especially in beginners.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Use easier gearing, shift early, reduce climbing intensity, and review fit if pain persists.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Tense grip and locked elbows reduce control and can contribute to hand, neck, shoulder, and crash risk.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Regress speed, add relaxation cues, check reach and contact points, and build trunk and shoulder endurance.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Hard front-brake or steering inputs on loose surfaces can cause front-wheel washout.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Brake earlier while upright, weight both wheels, choose firmer line, and reduce speed before features.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Fatigue degrades line holding, scanning, braking judgment, and group behavior.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Shorten route, choose easier group, add rest stops, and separate hard intervals from skill-learning rides.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Clip-in pedals can increase low-speed fall risk if start, stop, and emergency foot-down skills are not practiced.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Practice starts and stops on grass or an empty area, alternate lead foot, and use flat pedals until control is reliable.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Placing a rider into complex traffic before scanning, signaling, lane position, and junction skills are stable increases crash exposure.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Progress from traffic-free to simple roads before complex junctions, faster roads, or independent commuting routes.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Soft or muddy trails increase both environmental damage and rider traction risk.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Respect closures, choose durable surfaces or alternate ride options, and resume trail skills when conditions recover.

training_implications.name: Beginner confidence block
training_implications.recommendation: Start with short traffic-free sessions for starting, stopping, braking, straight-line control, scanning, signaling, and shifting before prescribing road endurance targets.

training_implications.name: Parking-lot skill microdose
training_implications.recommendation: Add 10 to 20 minutes of controlled braking, slalom, starts, stops, and one-hand signaling before easy rides for novice or returning riders.
progress_when: drills stay calm at low speed

training_implications.name: Group skill before race-like sessions
training_implications.recommendation: Require low-risk group riding practice before pacelines, fast club rides, criterium simulation, or mass-start MTB sessions.

training_implications.name: Descending progression
training_implications.recommendation: Progress descents by sight line, gradient, surface quality, corner count, traffic exposure, and rider relaxation rather than by route distance alone.

training_implications.name: Wet-weather substitution rule
training_implications.recommendation: If the planned outdoor ride includes rain, poor visibility, or loose surfaces beyond the rider's skill, substitute indoor endurance, traffic-free drills, or a flatter protected route.

training_implications.name: Cadence skill sessions
training_implications.recommendation: Use easy rides or indoor trainer sessions to teach cadence awareness, smooth pedaling, early shifting, and terrain anticipation before big-gear climbing work.

training_implications.name: Climbing technique before climbing volume
training_implications.recommendation: Teach pacing, early gear selection, seated economy, smooth pedaling, and traction before adding steep repeats or long mountain days.
progress_when: rider can restart safely on grade

training_implications.name: Assessment-based advancement
training_implications.recommendation: Advance level based on repeated safe execution of handling, traffic, group, and route tasks, not only mileage, power, or confidence.
progress_when: handling remains stable under mild fatigue

training_implications.name: Regression after crash or near miss
training_implications.recommendation: After a crash, fall, repeated skid, traffic conflict, or close group incident, temporarily regress to controlled drills and inspect bike, helmet, and confidence before resuming the prior plan.
progress_when: pain or concussion red flags are absent

training_implications.name: Route selection as a training variable
training_implications.recommendation: Route prescriptions should specify traffic complexity, surface, junction count, shoulder or bike-lane availability, lighting needs, gradient, and descent exposure.
progress_when: rider handles current route class safely
fatigue does not degrade line or scans

training_implications.name: Mandatory pre-ride check triggers
training_implications.recommendation: Require pre-ride checks after travel, wheel removal, maintenance, crashes, weather changes, new equipment, or before group, descent, traffic, and remote rides.
progress_when: rider can perform ABC Quick Check
rider knows when to seek mechanic support

training_implications.name: No fast group rides for beginners
training_implications.recommendation: Avoid fast group rides until the rider can hold line, brake smoothly, scan, signal, communicate hazards, and manage spacing without fatigue panic.
progress_when: rider can recover from small gaps

training_implications.name: Off-road surface ethics and safety
training_implications.recommendation: MTB and gravel plans should include trail-open status, surface durability, yield rules, passing communication, and self-sufficiency supplies before technical work.
progress_when: rider controls speed around blind corners
